title: review_log
description: One graded answer. APPEND-ONLY: never updated, never deleted, and kept when its card is deleted (marked orphaned instead) — this table is the only asset in the runtime model that cannot be regenerated, because it is the FSRS optimizer's entire training set and every scheduling field on `card` is replayable from it. FSRS-6 needs nothing per card beyond a stable id and this history: `Scheduler.review_card(card, rating, review_datetime)` in both reference implementations reads only (card, rating, timestamp), and the optimizer trains on the ordered (rating, elapsed) sequence per card. Everything beyond that here is stored to make a scheduling complaint debuggable. RUNTIME class: minted per learner, never committed to this repo. See design/user_state.md §3.

x-yomineko.note: Keyed on card_id, NEVER on the corpus item: an item fans out to up to five kinds (4,133 items -> 9,453 card instances), so design/srs_design.md §4's item-keyed review_log(user, ref, grade, elapsed, ts) would merge a recognition answer with a handwriting answer into one memory trace.

log_id.description: `rev:<opaque>`. Opaque and unordered on purpose — an ordering guarantee belongs to review_datetime, not to a key.

card_id.description: The card that was answered. Not declared as an IdRef because the card it names is runtime state, not a corpus record — the graph check has nothing to resolve it against.

rating.description: The FSRS grade: 1 Again, 2 Hard, 3 Good, 4 Easy. This and review_datetime are the ONLY two fields the algorithm requires. Kept as the integer the libraries use rather than as a word, so a log row can be handed to py-fsrs or ts-fsrs without a mapping table.

review_datetime.description: When the answer was graded, UTC. The second and last required FSRS input.

elapsed_days.description: Days since this card's previous review; 0 on the first. DERIVABLE from the review_datetime history and stored anyway, for two reasons: it is the column shape the Anki-format revlog and the FSRS optimizer's CSV both expect, and a stored value makes a replay's arithmetic checkable against what the scheduler actually saw.

scheduled_days.description: The interval the scheduler had asked for. `elapsed_days` minus this is how late or early the review was — the quantity FSRS handles natively and the one a scheduling complaint is almost always about.

state.description: The card's state AT REVIEW TIME, before this answer was applied. This is what lets a history be replayed exactly rather than approximately, and it is absent from both design sketches. Vocabulary owner: design — design/user_state.md#5-card. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

stability_after.description: The post-review S snapshot. Not an algorithm input — a witness. Without it, a replay that disagrees with the stored card cannot be localized to a review.

difficulty_after.description: The post-review D snapshot. Same purpose as stability_after.

due_after.description: The next due date this answer produced.

review_duration_ms.description: How long the answer took. Optional FSRS input (some variants use it); also the honest denominator for any time-per-card estimate in the daily budget.

source.description: Where the review came from. Costs nothing to store and is the difference between being able to debug a scheduling complaint and not: FSRS-6 models same-day reviews crudely, so same-day lesson drills must be distinguishable from queue reviews when training. Vocabulary owner: design — design/user_state.md#3-what-fsrs-6-actually-needs-and-why-card-is-a-cache. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

fsrs_version.description: Which algorithm graded this review. Rows from different versions coexist; a replay picks the scheduler by this field. Vocabulary owner: design — design/user_state.md#3-what-fsrs-6-actually-needs-and-why-card-is-a-cache. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

params_version.description: Which weight vector was in force.

orphaned.description: The card this row names no longer exists (content retired, or a kana card re-minted per glyph under D6). The row is KEPT and flagged rather than deleted: an optimizer's training set is not something to prune for tidiness.
